question: Under the principle of strict liability in anti-doping, who is ultimately responsible for any prohibited substance found in an athlete's body?
options: The athlete's coach or trainer
The athlete alone
The team physician or medical staff
The manufacturer of the supplement
explanation: Under strict liability, athletes are solely responsible for any substance found in their sample, regardless of how it entered their body or whether there was any intent to cheat.

question: What is the primary objective of clean sport education and anti-doping regulations?
options: To penalize as many competitors as possible
To protect athlete health and preserve fair and equal competition
To reduce the financial cost of sporting events
To restrict athletes from taking any prescription medicine
explanation: Clean sport protects athlete health, ensures fair play and integrity, and maintains trust in sport by preventing unethical advantages.

question: If an athlete is recommended a dietary supplement by a teammate or social media influencer, what should the athlete do first?
options: Take it immediately if it is labeled '100% all natural'
Verify its ingredients and consult official anti-doping resources or a qualified sports medical professional
Only take half the recommended dosage to stay safe
Assume dietary supplements are never prohibited
explanation: Supplements can contain undeclared prohibited substances or contaminants. 'Natural' does not guarantee prohibited-substance-free status. Always verify and consult official resources.

question: Which of the following is considered an Anti-Doping Rule Violation (ADRV)?
options: Eating a balanced nutritional meal before a competition
Evading, refusing, or failing to submit to sample collection without compelling justification
Asking a Doping Control Officer for identification
Taking an approved medication verified as non-prohibited
explanation: Evading, refusing, or failing to submit to sample collection is an Anti-Doping Rule Violation under WADA and NADA India regulations.

question: Why is it important for athletes to keep an accurate record of all medications and supplements they consume?
options: To declare them accurately during doping control paperwork and protect against contamination risks
It is only required for international Olympic medalists
To share their personal diet on public social media accounts
Because anti-doping agencies require daily receipts for grocery shopping
explanation: Recording all medications and supplements enables accurate declaration on the Doping Control Form (DCF), which is essential during testing and results management.

question: During doping control, what right does an athlete have regarding the testing personnel?
options: The right to inspect the official identification and authorization of the Doping Control Officer (DCO)
The right to choose any convenient date next week for sample collection
The right to take the sample in complete private without any observation
The right to replace the sample with another person's sample
explanation: Athletes have the right to see official identification and authorization from the DCO or chaperone before proceeding with sample collection.

question: Can an athlete request a representative or an interpreter to accompany them during the doping control process?
options: No, only the athlete and the DCO are ever allowed in the station
Yes, athletes have the right to be accompanied by a representative and, if available, an interpreter
Only if the athlete is under 12 years of age
Only after the sample has been sealed and sent to the laboratory
explanation: Athletes are entitled to be accompanied by a representative (and an interpreter if needed) to observe the process and assist them.

question: What is the responsibility of Athlete Support Personnel (coaches, doctors, physiotherapists)?
options: To help athletes find undetected performance-enhancing substances
To understand anti-doping policies, promote clean sport values, and cooperate with anti-doping organizations
They have no legal or ethical anti-doping obligations
To take samples on behalf of the athlete when the athlete is busy
explanation: Support personnel must know and comply with anti-doping rules, guide athletes responsibly, and never assist or encourage doping.

question: If an athlete has concerns or notices an irregularity during sample collection, where should they document it?
options: In the comments section of the Doping Control Form (DCF) before signing
Only on social media after returning home
They are not allowed to record concerns anywhere
In a handwritten letter sent 6 months later
explanation: Athletes have the right to record any comments or concerns directly on the Doping Control Form before signing.

question: What is an athlete's responsibility regarding 'Whereabouts' information when included in a testing pool?
options: Provide accurate, up-to-date location details so they can be located for unannounced out-of-competition testing
Share location only during competition days
Whereabouts details are optional and carry no penalty if missed
Only submit hotel receipts after a tournament ends
explanation: Athletes in registered testing pools must provide timely and accurate Whereabouts information to facilitate unannounced out-of-competition testing.

question: Once an athlete is officially notified for doping control, what must happen until the testing process is completed?
options: The athlete must remain under direct, continuous observation by the DCO or chaperone
The athlete can leave unchaperoned to attend a press conference and return hours later
The athlete can go home first to shower and rest
The chaperone waits outside the building without line of sight
explanation: From initial notification until the sample collection process is completed, the athlete must remain within direct sight of the DCO or chaperone.

question: Who selects the sample collection vessel and kit used for urine collection?
options: The DCO selects it and hands it open to the athlete
The athlete personally selects a sealed kit from a choice of multiple intact kits
The event organizer assigns a pre-opened container
The team coach must choose the equipment
explanation: The athlete must personally choose from a selection of intact, sealed collection vessels to ensure the integrity of the equipment.

question: How is a urine sample divided during sample collection?
options: All urine is poured into one single plastic cup
It is divided between an 'A' bottle (for initial analysis) and a 'B' bottle (for confirmatory analysis)
It is mixed with chemical stabilizers by the coach
Half is discarded immediately and the rest is kept in a test tube
explanation: The sample is divided into Bottle A (analyzed first) and Bottle B (stored for confirmatory testing if needed), both sealed by the athlete.

question: What should the athlete check before sealing the sample bottles?
options: That the unique sample code number on the bottles, caps, and documentation all match perfectly
That the athlete's name is written on the bottle glass
That the liquid is completely transparent
That the coach signs the bottle labels with a permanent marker
explanation: To preserve anonymity, the athlete's name does NOT appear on the bottle; instead, a unique code is used. The athlete must confirm that code numbers on bottles, caps, and paperwork match.

question: What happens if an athlete provides an insufficient volume of urine for a complete sample?
options: The test is cancelled and declared void
A partial sample procedure is followed, sealing the partial sample until more volume is provided
The athlete is automatically suspended for 2 years
Water is added to the bottle to reach the required volume
explanation: Under partial sample protocol, the provided amount is sealed and securely stored under observation until the athlete can provide sufficient volume to meet the minimum requirement.

question: What is the WADA Prohibited List?
options: A list of recommended gym workout routines
The international standard identifying substances and methods prohibited in-competition, at all times, or in specific sports
A list of athletes banned from travelling abroad
A commercial catalog of approved vitamin brands
explanation: The WADA Prohibited List is an updated international standard detailing which substances and methods are prohibited in sport, and under what conditions.

question: What is NADA India's 'Know Your Medicine' (KYM) service used for?
options: Buying discounted generic medications online
Checking whether a specific medicine or ingredient contains substances prohibited under anti-doping rules
Booking hospital appointments with sports surgeons
Diagnosing chronic sports injuries
explanation: KYM is an official NADA India tool that helps athletes and coaches check the prohibitory status of medicines and pharmaceutical ingredients.

question: What must an athlete do if they have an illness or condition that requires treatment with a prohibited substance?
options: Take the medicine secretly and hope they are not tested
Apply for a Therapeutic Use Exemption (TUE) before competing, following official procedures
Ask a coach to provide written permission on letterhead
Post an apology on social media
explanation: A Therapeutic Use Exemption (TUE) allows an athlete to use a necessary prohibited medication for legitimate medical reasons without committing an anti-doping rule violation.

question: Which category of substances is prohibited at all times (both in-competition and out-of-competition)?
options: S1 Anabolic Agents and S2 Peptide Hormones
S6 Stimulants (only prohibited in-competition)
S7 Narcotics (only prohibited in-competition)
P1 Beta-blockers in general sports
explanation: Classes S0 through S5, including S1 Anabolic Agents and S2 Peptide Hormones, are prohibited at all times (in-competition and out-of-competition).

question: Are methods such as chemical tampering, blood manipulation, and intravenous infusions subject to anti-doping restrictions?
options: No, only swallowed tablets and powders are restricted
Yes, prohibited methods (M1, M2, M3) are banned at all times under the Prohibited List
Only if performed on the exact day of a final medal match
Only for athletes competing in water sports
explanation: Prohibited methods (M1 Blood Manipulation, M2 Chemical and Physical Manipulation, M3 Gene Doping) are banned at all times under WADA and NADA regulations.

question: Under strict liability, what is the athlete's duty regarding anything they consume?
options: Trust product labels without independent verification
Ensure that no prohibited substance enters their body by thoroughly checking ingredients
Rely entirely on teammate recommendations
Assume prescription drugs from a family doctor are automatically exempt
explanation: Athletes are strictly liable for what is inside their sample, meaning they must ensure that no prohibited substance enters their body.

question: When does the in-competition testing period generally begin unless specified otherwise?
options: At 11:59 p.m. on the day before a competition in which the athlete is scheduled to participate
10 minutes before the starting whistle
Immediately after the medal ceremony
Only during the semifinal and final rounds
explanation: Under the World Anti-Doping Code, the in-competition period generally starts at 11:59 p.m. on the day before the competition through the end of the competition and sample collection.

question: What is the key purpose of dividing a urine sample into Bottle A and Bottle B?
options: To test for male and female hormones separately
Bottle A is used for initial testing, while Bottle B is preserved to confirm or challenge findings if needed
One bottle is kept by the athlete as a souvenir
One bottle is discarded if the first one passes
explanation: The B sample provides an essential safeguard for the athlete, allowing independent confirmatory testing if the A sample yields an adverse analytical finding.

question: What information should an athlete write on the Doping Control Form regarding recent medications?
options: All prescription medications, over-the-counter medicines, and supplements taken in the last 7 days
Only medications prescribed by an official Olympic doctor
No medications should ever be mentioned on the form
Only illegal street drugs
explanation: The athlete should declare all prescription and non-prescription medicines, vitamins, and supplements taken over the preceding 7 days on the Doping Control Form.

question: If an athlete requires an asthma inhaler containing a beta-2 agonist, what should they verify?
options: Check whether the specific active substance, dose, and route are permitted or require a TUE under the Prohibited List
Assume all inhalers are universally banned
Assume all inhalers are universally unrestricted
Use it only if purchased in another country
explanation: Certain beta-2 agonists have specific permitted dosing thresholds (like salbutamol under specified limits), while others are prohibited or require a TUE. Always check official rules.

question: Who has the authority to request a sample from an athlete?
options: Any fan or spectator at the venue
Authorized Anti-Doping Organizations (ADOs) such as NADA India, WADA, or International Federations
Commercial sports gear sponsors
Local law enforcement officers without anti-doping accreditation
explanation: Testing authority belongs exclusively to recognized Anti-Doping Organizations like NADA India, WADA, and authorized international/national sports federations.

question: What should an athlete do if a Doping Control Officer arrives for an out-of-competition test while training?
options: Refuse the test because it is not a tournament day
Cooperate immediately, show identification, and remain in sight of the testing official
Run away to avoid interruption of training
Demand to postpone the test until the next week
explanation: Out-of-competition testing can happen unannounced anytime and anywhere. Refusing or evading is a serious anti-doping rule violation.

question: Which of the following describes 'blood doping' or blood manipulation (Class M1)?
options: Drinking electrolyte fluids after a marathon
Administering or reintroducing red blood cells or blood products to unnaturally increase oxygen delivery to muscles
Having a standard routine blood test at a diagnostic clinic
Donating blood to a hospital blood bank
explanation: Blood manipulation to artificially enhance oxygen uptake or transport capacity is strictly prohibited under Class M1 of the Prohibited List.

question: What protection ensures that the laboratory testing a sample does not know the athlete's personal identity?
options: The lab receives only the anonymous sample code number, not the athlete's name or personal contact info
The sample is disguised inside a gift box
The DCO invents a fake athlete name on the bottle
There is no anonymity in sample testing
explanation: The laboratory copy of the Doping Control Form and the sample bottles contain only the unique code number, ensuring blind and unbiased laboratory analysis.

question: Where can Indian athletes access trusted, official information on clean sport, banned substances, and anti-doping procedures?
options: Anonymous forums and bodybuilding chatrooms
NADA India's official website (nadaindia.yas.gov.in) and WADA resources
Foreign online pharmacies selling unverified supplements
Unverified social media fitness reels
explanation: Official anti-doping guidance should always be sourced from NADA India (nadaindia.yas.gov.in) and WADA (wada-ama.org).
